text: After deployment and the end of turn, the turn is over. The next turn begins with the planning phase.

text: When the turn is over, the initiative token is passed to the next player clockwise. In 1v1 and team games this means the initiative alternates between the teams every turn.

examples.text: In 1v1, the player who did not have the initiative this turn has it next turn, and attacks first in its battle phase. (illustrative)
The player without the initiative this turn has it once the turn ends, declares the first attack of the next battle, and the turn after that it passes back.

text: Draft packs are passed in the draft step: each player passes their pack clockwise to the next player when they finish drafting, and the draft step is complete once all players have passed their pack. The end-of-turn passing of "any draft packs" with the initiative names this same pass; a pack is not passed a second time when the turn ends.

notes: The printed sources disagree on WHEN the pack passes: Manual p.16 and Rulebook 2023 p.6 (pages not in the U09 pack; added from the U08 pack/extract) put it in the draft step; Manual p.26 and Rulebook 2023 p.5 list "any draft packs" with the initiative at turn end. The rule follows the detailed draft section, reading the turn-end listing as the same pass (the p.16 N+1 refresh cycle only works with one pass per turn): that reconciliation is ours, hence basis mixed. D-U09-10. The engine passes when every seat has committed its draft (verifier probes r1/r2; engine entries are the verifier's measurement, not read by the drafter). Draft detail is 503 (U08).

text: The initiative token is not a token. An effect that refers to tokens never affects it.

examples.text: Download, which takes a token, cannot take the initiative. (illustrative)

notes: The RAQ note marks this untestable: the initiative is not an object an effect could be offered.
untestableReason: the initiative is a seat index in the game state, not an object any effect could reach, so no state could show it being treated as a token
